# 4-Day Budget Lisbon Getaway for 2 Adults

A walkable, history-rich Lisbon plan built around neighborhoods, seafood, and one museum-focused day. I’m assuming a mid-range budget style, using public transit plus plenty of walking, and keeping meals under **€25 per person per meal**.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Itinerary
### Day 1: Alfama, Baixa, and the riverfront
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Start in **Alfama** with a self-guided walk from Sé Cathedral to Miradouro de Santa Luzia and Portas do Sol.
- Afternoon: Explore **Baixa** and **Rua Augusta**, then walk to Praça do Comércio and the Cais do Sodré waterfront.
- Evening: Dinner in Alfama or nearby with grilled fish or sardines; end with a relaxed fado-adjacent neighborhood stroll.
- Local transport: **€0–€6 total** if mostly walking; add one tram/metro ride if needed.
- Meal ideas: breakfast pastry + coffee (**€6–€10 pp**), lunch at a tasca (**€12–€18 pp**), seafood dinner (**€18–€25 pp**).

### Day 2: Belém and the museum day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Go to **Belém** early for Jerónimos Monastery exterior, Belém Tower area, and the river promenade.
- Afternoon: Choose your museum focus: **Museu Nacional do Azulejo** if you want classic Lisbon culture, or **MAAT** for a modern art/architecture contrast.
- Evening: Return to central Lisbon for a simple dinner near Chiado or Cais do Sodré.
- Local transport: **€6–€12 total** for tram/metro/bus round trips.
- Meal ideas: pastel de nata stop + coffee (**€4–€8 pp**), museum-area lunch (**€12–€20 pp**), dinner with seafood rice or octopus (**€18–€25 pp**).

### Day 3: Bairro Alto, Chiado, and Príncipe Real
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Walk through **Chiado** and **Príncipe Real**, with time for viewpoints and small squares.
- Afternoon: Browse bookstores, tiled facades, and design shops; take a break at Jardim do Príncipe Real.
- Evening: Head to **Bairro Alto** for dinner, then enjoy the atmosphere without overplanning the night.
- Local transport: **€0–€8 total**; one short metro or funicular ride if you want to save energy.
- Meal ideas: brunch or late breakfast (**€10–€15 pp**), light lunch (**€12–€18 pp**), casual dinner with shared starters and fish main (**€18–€25 pp**).

### Day 4: Mouraria, viewpoints, and a slow final day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Walk **Mouraria** and nearby viewpoints for a less polished but very local Lisbon feel.
- Afternoon: Leave room for a flexible choice: revisit a favorite district, shop for souvenirs, or do a final riverfront walk.
- Evening: Farewell dinner in central Lisbon with seafood or grilled meats, then a calm last-night stroll.
- Local transport: **€0–€10 total** depending on how much walking you do.
- Meal ideas: café breakfast (**€6–€10 pp**), neighborhood lunch (**€12–€18 pp**), final dinner (**€18–€25 pp**).

## Budget Plan for 2 Adults
### Estimated Trip Spend
| Category | Estimated Cost | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Lodging, 3 nights | €360–€540 | Budget hotel or well-located apartment |
| Local transport | €25–€50 | Metro, tram, bus, occasional taxi |
| Meals | €300–€480 | 2 people, keeping meals under €25 pp |
| Attractions | €60–€140 | Museum entry + a few paid sights |
| Coffee, snacks, extras | €80–€140 | Pastries, drinks, small treats |
| Total | **€825–€1,350** | Target stays on budget with modest lodging |

### Budget-Friendly Target
- Best value lodging target: **€120–€150 per night**
- Daily food target for 2: **€60–€80**
- Daily transport target for 2: **€5–€15**
- Attraction target: **1 paid major sight + free walking areas**

## Rainy-Day Backup Plan
### Museum-and-Café Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cloud-rain.svg
- Start at **Museu Nacional do Azulejo** or **MAAT** depending on your interest.
- Spend the wettest hours in **Chiado** bookstores, cafés, and arcades.
- Add an indoor lunch in Baixa or Cais do Sodré.
- If the rain continues, switch the evening to a long seafood dinner and a relaxed transit-based return.

### Good rainy substitutions
- National Tile Museum instead of longer walking routes
- Time Out Market for an easy indoor food stop
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/83/Lobster%2C_Time_Out_Market_Lisboa_%2850661858143%29.jpg Alt=Time Out Market for an easy indoor food stop, Lisbon, Portugal
- Tram/metro loops between districts instead of hill walks
- Café-hopping in Chiado and Príncipe Real

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Check transit] https://www.metrolisboa.pt/en/
Action: [Button: Museum tickets] https://www.museudoazulejo.gov.pt/
Action: [Button: Lisbon tourism] https://www.visitlisboa.com/

## Sources
- Lisbon Metro: https://www.metrolisboa.pt/en/
- Visit Lisboa: https://www.visitlisboa.com/
- Museu Nacional do Azulejo: https://www.museudoazulejo.gov.pt/
